# 4.7 Electromagnetism

### Magnetic Field Lines
- This allows us to find the direction of a magnetic field
- The field goes from North Out, to South in a Closed Loop
- The closer the line is the higher the strength
- Field lines will never intersect (since they can never point in two directions at the same time)

#### Magnetic Field and Current + Right Hand rule....
- The stronger the **current** the stronger the **magnetic field**
- Magnetic fields weakens with distance
- Field lines can be seen as concentric circles (centred at the wire)

##### Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
- Recall: Newtons 3rd law, for every action they are is a equal and opposite reaction
- We can then infer that: 
	- **More current** $\rightarrow$ More Force, 
	- The maximum force is when the wire is perpendicular ($\perp$) to the magnetic field
	- The direction of the force acting on the wire depends on direction of the **current** and the direction of the **field**
##### Comparing Magnetic and Electric Forces
- $F_{mag} = q(\vec{V} \times \vec{B}) \rightarrow q\Vert{\vec{V} \Vert \vec{B}} \Vert sin\theta$ (Magnetic Force)
- $F_{elec} = q\vec{E}$ 
- $F_{max} = \vec{V} \perp \vec{B}$  
- $F_{min} = \vec{V} \parallel \vec{B}$ or $\vec{V} = 0$
